text:
ali: Pushed a new embedding variant to staging: nightjar-small (int8 per-channel) vs baseline heron-v2 (fp16). Running recall@k and clustering checks on the short-query holdout. Noticing cluster splits on a couple topical shards — leaning odd. Anyone else digging in?

marta: I pulled the staging metrics. Recall@1 dropped ~2.1% on short queries, recall@10 ~0.9%. Silhouette score for a few topics decreased from 0.42 -> 0.29.

ryan: hmm, did we use the same mean-centering / l2 norm preprocessing for both? small models sometimes flip norms if postproc differs.

ali: yep same preprocessing pipeline. I re-ran with and without l2 norm, little change. suspect quantization noise on narrow queries.

devon: can you paste the eval command you ran? i'll replicate locally.

ali: sure — command below.

```bash
./eval_embeddings.py --model nightjar-small --holdout short_queries.jsonl --k 1,3,10 --norm l2 --output out/nightjar_short_k.json
```

marta: curious if batch-size at encoding changed. I noticed runtimes used batch 512 in hosted but local eval used 64 which could change kv-cache warmup.

ryan: try forcing small batch (64) and large (512) both — if recall differs, might be nondeterminism with batching/float accumulation.

ali: ran both. no meaningful recall delta (<0.1%). so probably quantization.

sasha: did we test per-tensor int8 vs per-channel int8? Per-channel usually preserves similarity better for conv/embedding matrices.

ali: nightjar-small was built per-channel. i also tried per-tensor earlier — per-tensor was worse (recall@1 -3.4%). per-channel still shows the silhouette drop.

eval-bot: quick summarize: nightjar-small (int8 per-channel): recall@1 -2.1, recall@10 -0.9, silhouette -0.13 vs heron-v2(fp16). Suggested next steps: run holdout stratified by query length + human spot-check top-5 mismatches.

devon: i sliced results by topic and found two topics (legal-docs, api-howto) with biggest drift. For legal-docs the nearest neighbor grads look semantically off — sometimes returning procedural templates instead of precedents.

marta: can you dump a few examples? paste 2-3 pairs (query -> top1/top3).

devon: pasted below (redacted):
- "what is the statute of limitations for X?" -> nightjar top1: "how to file a complaint form" (bad), heron top1: "statute of limitations for X is Y" (good)
- "api returns 500 on upload" -> nightjar top3 includes unrelated pagination docs, heron returns error handling snippets.

ali: thanks — that helps. hypothesis: nightjar's embedding heads emphasize surface-level tokens that quantization pushes over deeper predicate signals for short queries.

ryan: mitigation ideas: try mixed-precision for the last projection layer (keep fp16 for final dense) or KD-calib (tiny retrain on holdout). Also evaluate cosine vs dot product; sometimes metric choice interacts with quant noise.

ali: i'll run a quick mixed-precision build (fp16 final proj) and rerun. ETA ~90m. posting logs here when done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sasha: also worth running cluster-UMAP visual quicklook; if embeddings collapse along one axis that's a sign of quant-induced scale shifts. i can spin that up if you push the out JSON to s3.

ali: pushed out/nightjar_short_k.json to s3://redwood-staging/nightjar/3801234567/ — gave sasha write link.

sasha: grabbing it now. will post umap image in thread when ready.

marta: one more ask — add recall@k per-length bucket (<=8 tokens, 9-32, >32). short queries mainly <=8 so we can quantify sensitivity.

eval-bot: noted. scheduled length-bucketed eval job: job-3801234600. will post results when complete.

ryan: thanks all. if mixed-precision fixes >50% of the recall gap, we can consider shipping a per-model precision override in the catalog. otherwise fall back to heron-v2 for short-query workloads.

ali: update: mixed-precision run finished — initial numbers: recall@1 gap reduced from -2.1% -> -0.8%. silhouette delta now -0.05. uploading full artifacts in ~10m.

marta: that's promising. can we run a small human eval on the 50 most changed queries? i'll coordinate. :white_check_mark:

devon: i'll prepare the 50 diff set and tag legal/doc-owner + api-owners for review.

sasha: umap looks like clusters mostly preserved. earlier tear in legal cluster is less pronounced in mixed-precision. posting image link: https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-staging/nightjar/3801234567/umap_mixedprecision.png

ali: great progress — thanks team. will hold staging until human review comes back.

marta: filing a short postmortem note in the onboarding doc: model-nightjar-small -> quant-int8-per-channel + mixed-precision mitigation.

ryan: nice work. small reminder to add the model's quant config to the model catalog entry so runtime can route short-query traffic to heron-v2 until we decide.

ali: on it. stopping here. :party_popper:
